chunks: 2441 - Shihāb ibn ʿAbd Rabbih narrated, saying:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: You know my condition, the extent of my means, and my generosity toward my brothers. I accompany a group of them on the road to Makkah and spend generously on them.

He said: “Do not do that, O Shihāb. If you are generous and they also spend, you will overburden them; and if they hold back, you will humiliate them. So accompany your equals, accompany your equals.”

key_terms.أَجْحَفْتَ بِهِمْ: you would impose hardship on them or strain them unfairly
key_terms.أَذْلَلْتَهُمْ: you would humiliate them or make them feel low
key_terms.إِخْوَانِي: my brothers, meaning fellow believers or companions
key_terms.سَعَةَ يَدِي: my financial capacity or material means
key_terms.طَرِيقِ مَكَّةَ: the road to Makkah, indicating travel for hajj or visitation
key_terms.نُظَرَاءَكَ: those who are your equals in means or social standing

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام tell Shihāb not to spend generously on his travel companions to Makkah?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches sensitivity in financial dealings among companions during travel, especially on the way to Makkah. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام advises that excessive generosity can either pressure others beyond their means or leave them feeling diminished. The teaching emphasizes preserving dignity, balance, and mutual ease in companionship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2441 - Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih narrated:

I said to Abu Abdullah (as): "You know my situation, my financial capacity, and how I spend generously on my brothers. Sometimes I accompany a group of them on the road to Mecca and provide generously for them."

Imam (as) said: "Do not do that, O Shihab. If you are generous and they are generous as well, you will burden them. And if they withhold, you will humiliate them. Instead, travel with those who are your equals. Travel with those who are your equals."
